# `nish/json-tokenizer`

A validating, streaming tokenizer for RFC 8259 JSON held in a window of a `u8[]`.

```ts
import {
  JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
  JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_NUMBER_BYTES,
  JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_STRING_BYTES,
  JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES,
  JSON_TOK_ARRAY_BEGIN,
  JSON_TOK_ARRAY_END,
  JSON_TOK_END,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_CONTROL,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_DEPTH,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_ESCAPE,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_NUMBER,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_NUMBER_LIMIT,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_STRING_LIMIT,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_SURROGATE,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_SYNTAX,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_TOTAL_LIMIT,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_TRAILING,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_TRUNCATED,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_UTF8,
  JSON_TOK_ERR_WINDOW,
  JSON_TOK_FALSE,
  JSON_TOK_KEY,
  JSON_TOK_NULL,
  JSON_TOK_NUMBER,
  JSON_TOK_OBJECT_BEGIN,
  JSON_TOK_OBJECT_END,
  JSON_TOK_STRING,
  JSON_TOK_TRUE,
  JsonLimits,
  JsonTokenizer,
} from "nish/json-tokenizer";
```

```ts
import { JsonLimits, JsonTokenizer, JSON_TOK_END, JSON_TOK_KEY } from "nish/json-tokenizer";

const t = new JsonTokenizer(body, 0, toI32(body.length), new JsonLimits());
let k: i32 = t.next();
while (k > 0) {
  if (k === JSON_TOK_KEY && t.keyEquals("message")) {
    // t.next() is the value; t.stringInto(out, 0) copies it out
  }
  k = t.next();
}
// k === JSON_TOK_END: the window held one whole, valid JSON text
// k < 0: a JSON_TOK_ERR_* code, also in t.failed, at byte t.errorAt
```

<scalar-callout type="info">

`std/json`'s `jsonField` reads one field of one flat object and validates
nothing. A server that takes JSON from a peer needs the opposite: every byte
checked against the grammar, nothing allocated per request, and a hard limit
on everything an attacker controls. That is this module.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="One token per `next()`">

It answers a `JSON_TOK_*` kind — an object or
array opening or closing, a key, a string, a number, `true`, `false` or
`null` — then `JSON_TOK_END` once the top-level value is complete and only
blanks follow it, and `JSON_TOK_END` again on every later call.
`tokStart` and `tokEnd` bound the token's bytes in the source (a string's
include its quotes), and `depth` is the number of containers open after it.
Structure is checked as the tokens go by: a comma or colon out of place, a
closer that does not match its opener, a second top-level value, or anything
but blanks after the first, is an error at the byte where it stands.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Errors are sticky">

The first error sets `failed` to a negative
`JSON_TOK_ERR_*` code and `errorAt` to the byte offset it was found at, and
every later `next()` answers the same code without reading anything, as
`nish/net/hpack`'s decoder does. Nothing an input can hold panics, and no
byte outside `src[off, off + len)` is ever read. `reset` starts over on a new
window with the same limits and the same depth stack, so a server holds one
tokenizer per connection and allocates nothing per request.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Strings are checked as UTF-8 and decoded on request">

A string may hold
any well-formed UTF-8 (RFC 3629: no overlong form, no surrogate code point,
nothing past U+10FFFF, no sequence cut short), no raw byte below 0x20, and
the escapes of RFC 8259 §7. A `\u` escape of a high surrogate must be
followed at once by one of a low surrogate, and a low surrogate must follow
a high one: a lone surrogate escape is an error. RFC 8259 allows one, but it
names no Unicode character, decodes to no valid UTF-8, and is what a peer
smuggles past a check done on the decoded bytes, so this module takes the
stricter reading (`docs/security/json.md`, "Lone surrogates"). Nothing is decoded until
the caller asks: `stringInto` writes the decoded bytes of the current key
or string into the caller's array, and `keyEquals` compares them with a
string without writing them anywhere.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Numbers are checked against the grammar and parsed on request">

`numberF64` is correctly rounded, ties to even, in one of three ways. A
number of at most 19 significant digits is read into a `u64`. When that is
at most 2^53 and the decimal exponent is within ±22, the answer is one exact
multiply or divide of two exact doubles (Clinger's fast path). Any other
number of at most 19 digits is the Eisel–Lemire algorithm as fast_float
computes it: one or two 64×64-bit products with a truncated power of five,
which Mushtak and Lemire prove always decide the rounding for so few digits,
so it never needs a fallback. A number of more digits, or with an exponent
past `JSON_TOK_EXPONENT_CAP`, goes to the runtime's `parseFloat`, which is
`strtod`, from a function whose own arena scope releases the copy it reads,
so it leaves the arena where it was. `isInteger` and `numberI64` read a number
written without a fraction or an exponent that fits in an `i64`, and
`isU64` and `numberU64` one written without a sign either that fits in a
`u64`. Those go by spelling; `isIntegral` asks whether the value is whole,
however it is written (`1.0`, `1e2`), from the text and at any size.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Runs are read in bulk">

A string's plain bytes, the blanks between
tokens and a number's digits are each stepped over by a loop that reads
`src` directly, bounded by the window's end (or a string's or number's
limit, which is never past it) and by the array's length, so a run stops
exactly where a read through `jsonTokByteAt` would have answered `-1`.
The readers of a number already scanned, and `stringInto`'s copy of a
string with no escape, read `src` the same way; every other byte goes
through `jsonTokByteAt`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Duplicate keys are tokens">

`{"a":1,"a":2}` is two keys; which one wins,
or whether a duplicate is an error, is the decision of whatever reads the
tokens (`docs/security/json.md`, JSON-3).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**The limits** are `JsonLimits`: nesting depth, bytes in one string, bytes
in one number and bytes in the whole window. Each has its own error code and
a default sized for a request body, and each is checked before the work it
bounds, so a depth bomb costs one byte of stack per level allowed and an
over-long string is refused at the first byte past the limit.

</scalar-callout>

Every name here is `json`-prefixed, because a `std/` module is compiled into
the program that imports it and the symbol namespace is flat
(`std/README.md`). Every offset is a byte offset, and every constant is an
`i32`, so the module is the same under `--number-mode f64`
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §4). Written from RFC 8259 and RFC 3629, except
`numberF64`'s Eisel–Lemire path and its table of powers of five, which are
adapted from fast_float under the notice above `jsonTokW64`.

## JsonLimits

What a `JsonTokenizer` refuses to read, each with its own error code. The
tokenizer copies the four numbers when it is made, so changing an object
afterwards changes nothing for a tokenizer already made from it. A negative
limit is read as zero: with a depth of zero only a scalar top-level value
is accepted, with a string limit of zero only `""`.

```ts
class JsonLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new JsonLimits()` | The defaults, `JSON_DEFAULT_*`. |
| `maxDepth: i32` | Containers open at once; the tokenizer allocates one byte of stack per level, once. |
| `maxNumberBytes: i32` | Bytes in one number, sign and exponent included. |
| `maxStringBytes: i32` | Raw bytes between a string's quotes, escapes counted as written. |
| `maxTotalBytes: i32` | Bytes in the window handed to the constructor or to `reset`. |

## JsonTokenizer

The tokenizer. One per connection or per document; `reset` reuses it, and
nothing it does after the constructor allocates, except `numberF64`'s
`parseFloat` path, which releases what it allocated before it returns.

The fields a caller reads are `depth`, `kind`, `tokStart`, `tokEnd`,
`failed` and `errorAt`. The rest are the cursor and what the scan of the
current token found, and are read through the methods.

```ts
class JsonTokenizer
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new JsonTokenizer(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, limits: JsonLimits)` | A tokenizer over `src[off, off + len)` held to `limits`. A negative limit counts as 0, and the depth stack is allocated here, once, `maxDepth` bytes long, and `reset` reuses it. |
| `depth: i32` | Containers open after the current token. |
| `errorAt: i32` | The byte offset in `src` the error was found at, and `-1` until one. Read it only once `failed` is set: a `JSON_TOK_ERR_WINDOW` records the `off` the caller passed, which may itself be negative or past the end of `src`. |
| `failed: i32` | The sticky error, a negative `JSON_TOK_ERR_*` code; `0` until one. |
| `integral: boolean` | Whether the current number is written with neither a fraction nor an exponent: the spelling, so `1.0` is not. `isIntegral()` reads the value. |
| `kind: i32` | The current token's kind, the last `next()` answered; `JSON_TOK_END` before the first. |
| `src: u8[]` | The bytes being read. The tokenizer never writes them. |
| `tokEnd: i32` | One past the current token's last byte; see `tokStart`. |
| `tokStart: i32` | The current token's bytes, `src[tokStart, tokEnd)`; a string's and a key's include their quotes. |
| `isInteger(): boolean` | Whether the current token is a number written without a fraction or an exponent whose value fits in an `i64`: `-0` and `9223372036854775807` are, `1.0`, `1e2` and `9223372036854775808` are not. That is the spelling rule; `isIntegral()` asks whether the value is whole. |
| `isIntegral(): boolean` | Whether the current token is a number whose value is a whole number, however it is written: JSON Schema 2020-12's "integer". `-0.0`, `1.0`, `1e2`, `100e-2` and `1e400` are; `1.5`, `10e-2` and `1e-400` are not. It says nothing about fitting an `i64`, and it is not the `integral` field or `isInteger()`, which go by spelling and refuse `1.0` and `1e2`.<br><br>It reads the text, never an `f64`, so `12345678901234567890.0` and `1e400` answer exactly. With F fraction digits, z trailing zeros across all the digits and the exponent E, the value is whole when every digit is zero or E - F + z >= 0. F and z count bytes of the token, so F - z fits an `i32` whatever the limits, and `jsonTokDigitsExceed` compares E with it without adding up more of E than it needs, so `1e99999999999` answers too. |
| `isText(): boolean` | Whether the current token is a key or a string. |
| `isU64(): boolean` | Whether the current token is a number written in digits alone, with no sign, fraction or exponent, whose value fits in a `u64`: `0` and `18446744073709551615` are; `-0`, `-1`, `1.0`, `1e2` and `18446744073709551616` are not. |
| `keyEquals(name: string): boolean` | Whether the current key or string, decoded, is exactly `name`'s bytes; `false` when the token is neither. Nothing is allocated or written. `name.length` and `charCodeAt` are bytes natively. Under Node they are UTF-16 code units, compared one by one against the decoded UTF-8 bytes: an ASCII name answers the same both ways, a genuine non-ASCII name does not match there, and a name whose code units 0x80 to 0xFF spell those bytes does (`"Ã©"` matches a key `"é"`). That is the bytes against code units divergence `docs/wp33-round-trip.md` §3.2 records. |
| `next(): i32` | The next token's kind, `JSON_TOK_END`, or a negative error, which is sticky. |
| `numberF64(): f64` | The current number as the nearest `f64`, ties to even, as `JSON.parse` reads it: `-0` is negative zero, a magnitude past the largest double is an infinity and one below the smallest is zero. `0` when the current token is not a number. |
| `numberI64(): i64` | The current number as an `i64` when `isInteger()` holds, and `0` otherwise. Read it after checking `isInteger()`: a `0` alone does not say which. |
| `numberU64(): u64` | The current number as a `u64` when `isU64()` holds, and `0` otherwise. Read it after checking `isU64()`: a `0` alone does not say which. |
| `reset(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Starts over on `src[off, off + len)`, keeping the limits and the depth stack, and clearing any error. A window outside `src` or longer than the total limit is refused here, and the first `next()` answers it. |
| `skipValue(): i32` | Steps over the value the current token starts, so that the next `next()` answers what follows it. After a key, that is the key's value; after an opener, everything up to and including its closer; after a scalar or a closer, nothing. Answers the kind of the last token it read (the closer, or the scalar), or a negative error. |
| `stringInto(out: u8[], at: i32): i32` | Writes the current key's or string's decoded bytes to `out` from `at`, and answers how many; `-1`, writing nothing, when the current token is neither or `out` has fewer than `stringLength()` bytes from `at`. |
| `stringLength(): i32` | The current key's or string's length once decoded, or `-1` when the token is neither. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="128" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i32`

The default limits, sized for a request body. A depth of 128 is serde_json's
recursion limit and deeper than any document a person writes; a string may
be a mebibyte; 256 bytes hold every double in its shortest form many times
over; and a body of 16 MiB is past what an HTTP server should buffer anyway.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_NUMBER_BYTES: i32`

The default longest number text, in bytes: room for any double in its shortest form.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1,048,576" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_STRING_BYTES: i32`

The default longest string or key: a mebibyte of raw bytes between its
quotes, escapes counted as written.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16,777,216" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES: i32`

The default largest window, in bytes: a 16 MiB body.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ARRAY_BEGIN: i32`

`[`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ARRAY_END: i32`

`]`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_END: i32`

The top-level value is complete and only blanks follow it. Answered again on every later call.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_CONTROL: i32`

A raw byte below 0x20 inside a string, which RFC 8259 §7 requires to be escaped.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_DEPTH: i32`

An opening bracket or brace past `JsonLimits.maxDepth` open containers.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_ESCAPE: i32`

A backslash not followed by one of `"/bfnrt`, or a `\u` not followed by four hex digits.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_NUMBER: i32`

A number outside the RFC 8259 §6 grammar: `-a`, `1.a`, `1ex`, `-Infinity`. A number the window cuts short (`1.`, `-`) is `JSON_TOK_ERR_TRUNCATED`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_NUMBER_LIMIT: i32`

A number longer than `JsonLimits.maxNumberBytes` bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_STRING_LIMIT: i32`

A string, or a key, longer than `JsonLimits.maxStringBytes` bytes between its quotes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_SURROGATE: i32`

A `\u` escape of a surrogate that is not one half of a high-then-low pair.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_SYNTAX: i32`

A byte that cannot stand where it stands: `[1,]`, `{"a" 1}`, `[1}`, `[01]`, `+1`, `.5`, `nulx`, a byte outside a string that is not ASCII.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-12" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_TOTAL_LIMIT: i32`

A window longer than `JsonLimits.maxTotalBytes` bytes. Answered by the first `next()`, before anything is read.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_TRAILING: i32`

Something other than blanks after the top-level value: `[] []`, `1 2`, a trailing NUL.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_TRUNCATED: i32`

The window ended inside a value: an empty window, `[1,`, `{"a":`, an unclosed string.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_UTF8: i32`

A string holds a byte sequence that is not UTF-8: an overlong form, a surrogate, a code point past U+10FFFF, a sequence cut short by a byte that does not continue it, a stray continuation byte.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-13" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_ERR_WINDOW: i32`

`off` and `len` do not describe a window inside `src`. Answered by the first `next()`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_FALSE: i32`

`false`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_KEY: i32`

A member's name: a string followed by its colon. The value is the next token.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`JSON_TOK_NULL: i32`

`null`.

</scalar-card>

A number value.
